spec.title: DSP-API — Response Duration
spec.description: Request latency, throughput and server time for dsp-api, from the tapir request metrics (service_name=DSP_svc_api), plus the API-side Fuseki round-trip histogram. Durations are averages (rate(sum)/rate(count), phase=body): the histogram buckets are dropped by the ops-deploy scrape filter, so no percentiles yet. Requests that matched no endpoint (path="") are excluded everywhere. Route group / Route (path) / Method / Exclude routes scope the panels; Smoothing window is the rate() window of every time-series panel. Purple markers are container restarts. See grafana-dashboards/dsp-api/README.md for the query-shape rules.

legacyOptions.textFormat: The API container of at least one selected stack (re)started: its process CPU counter dropped. Deploys do this, but so do crashes, host reboots and manual restarts; with Stack = All on prod this includes ~30 RDU boxes.

spec.title: Response time (selected range): avg, p50 / p95 / p99
spec.description: Full-request duration (phase=body) over the dashboard range: avg = rate(sum)/rate(count), percentiles = histogram_quantile over rate(_bucket[$__range]). Scoped by the Route group, Method and Exclude routes filters. Requests that matched no endpoint (CORS OPTIONS preflights, HEAD probes; empty path label) are excluded. Percentiles come from tapir_request_duration_seconds_bucket, scraped since ops-deploy#1434 (stage from 2026-09-21, prod from 2026-09-23 ~06:00 UTC); earlier ranges show no percentile data. Buckets: 5, 10, 25, 50, 75, 100, 250, 500, 750 ms, 1, 2.5, 5, 7.5, 10, 15, 30, 45, 60 s; histogram_quantile() interpolates linearly inside a bucket and caps at 60 s.

spec.title: Request rate
spec.description: Requests per second over the dashboard range, scoped by Route group, Method and Exclude routes. Excluding /health and /version removes monitoring traffic. Requests that matched no endpoint (empty path label) are excluded.

spec.title: 5xx error rate (range)
spec.description: Share of requests with a 5xx status over the dashboard range, scoped by Route group, Method and Exclude routes. Requests that matched no endpoint (empty path label) are excluded.

spec.title: Response duration — global: avg, p50 / p95 / p99
spec.description: Full-request duration (phase=body) over time, scoped by Route group, Method and Exclude routes; rate() window = Smoothing window. avg = rate(sum)/rate(count) and has full history; the percentiles show how the tail moves independently of the mean (a rising p99 with a flat avg is a few very slow requests). Percentiles come from tapir_request_duration_seconds_bucket, scraped since ops-deploy#1434 (stage from 2026-09-21, prod from 2026-09-23 ~06:00 UTC); earlier ranges show no percentile data. Buckets: 5, 10, 25, 50, 75, 100, 250, 500, 750 ms, 1, 2.5, 5, 7.5, 10, 15, 30, 45, 60 s; histogram_quantile() interpolates linearly inside a bucket and caps at 60 s. The day/night swing is traffic mix (fast automated reads at night, human-driven searches by day), not health checks. Purple markers: dsp-api container restarts (deploys, but also crashes/reboots).

spec.title: Average response duration by route
spec.description: Mean full-request duration (phase=body) per route over time, within the Route group / Route (path) / Method / Exclude filters; rate() window = Smoothing window. Log2 y-axis so one slow, rare route does not flatten the rest. Purple markers: dsp-api container restarts (deploys, but also crashes/reboots).

spec.title: Slowest Gravsearch queries (traces)
spec.description: Individual gravsearch executions slower than the Duration ≥ threshold, from Tempo traces (service DSP_svc_api), scoped to the selected environment/stack. Sorted slowest first. To read the actual SPARQL/Gravsearch query: click the Trace ID → in the trace view select the 'gravsearch' span → Events → 'gravsearch.query' → db.query.text (verbatim, untruncated). Tempo returns the most recent matches above the threshold (limit 100), then this table sorts them by duration. Set 'Project shortcode (Gravsearch)' to filter to one project's queries (matches the ontology IRIs in the query text, host-agnostic; empty = all projects). The 'Query (preview)' column shows the start of the query inline (filtering on the event surfaces it); click the Trace ID for the full, untruncated text. The 'Project' column is the gravsearch.project_shortcodes span attribute (DEV-7031): the projects a query references, read from its ontology IRIs and its resource IRIs alike, so it is populated for dsp-api's internal searches (incoming links, still-image representations, incoming regions) as well. It is blank on traces recorded before that instrumentation was deployed. The 'Scoped to' column is gravsearch.project_restriction: the project the request explicitly limited the search to, so a row with a value there was a project-scoped search rather than a query that merely references the project. Advanced Search in dsp-app always sends one; most other callers do not, and empty means unrestricted rather than unknown. It is a project IRI, not a shortcode, so for projects created after shortcode-shaped IRIs were retired it will not visually match the Project column — see the runbook. Note that the 'Project shortcode (Gravsearch)' variable still filters on the query text, so it matches ontology IRIs only; prefer reading the Project column over trusting that filter for internal searches.

spec.query: { span:name = "gravsearch" && span.environment =~ "${environment:regex}" && span.stack =~ "${stack:regex}" && span:duration > ${gsthreshold} && event.db.query.text =~ ".*ontology/${project}.*" } | select(span:duration, span.gravsearch.query.shape, span.gravsearch.schema_predicates, span.gravsearch.project_shortcodes, span.gravsearch.project_restriction)

value.title: Open trace → gravsearch span → Events → gravsearch.query

spec.title: Average response duration by route group ($smoothing)
spec.description: Mean full-request duration per route group (same regexes as the Route group filter), one line each plus All; rate() window = Smoothing window. Separates "reads got slower" from "searches got slower", which the global average blurs. Honours Method and Exclude routes; ignores the Route group filter by design. Log2 y-axis. Purple markers: dsp-api container restarts (deploys, but also crashes/reboots).

spec.title: Routes ranked by total server time (range)
spec.description: Per route and method over the dashboard range: total server time (sum of all request durations), average duration, request count, 4xx and 5xx counts, sorted by total time. Total time is where optimisation pays off; the slowest-average routes are usually rare ones. Only routes that reported a request duration in the range appear. Click a path to open Tempo with that route's server spans slower than 1 s in the selected environment/stack. Honours Route group / Route (path) / Method / Exclude routes. p50/p95 are histogram_quantile over rate(_bucket[$__range]) per route and method; empty for ranges before the buckets were scraped (prod: before 2026-09-23 ~06:00 UTC).

query.query: { resource.service.name = "DSP_svc_api" && span:kind = server && span.http.route = "${__data.fields.path}" && span.environment =~ "${environment:regex}" && span.stack =~ "${stack:regex}" && span:duration > 1s }

spec.title: Server time per route — busy seconds per second ($smoothing)
spec.description: Seconds of request processing per second, per route, stacked (rate of the duration sum). Where the API spends its time; a fast but constantly called route can dominate. Compare with Requests per route below: server time that rises with requests is load, without them a slowdown. Same filters as the routes table; rate() window = Smoothing window. Purple markers: dsp-api container restarts (deploys, but also crashes/reboots).

spec.title: 5xx responses per route (count per plot step)
spec.description: Approximate number of 5xx responses per route per plot step, as stacked bars (increase() over one plot step). Read it for WHEN errors happened; for HOW MANY use the 5xx column of the routes table: increase() extrapolates sparse counts, so the legend total can exceed the table by about one per burst. Only routes with a 5xx in the range appear. Same filters as the routes table; per path.

spec.title: Triplestore round-trip p50 / p95 / p99 by kind ($smoothing)
spec.description: Latency of dsp-api's own SPARQL round trips to Fuseki (fuseki_request_duration, measured in dsp-api), Gravsearch vs everything else, p50/p95/p99; rate() window = Smoothing window. The histogram buckets are decades (10 ms, 100 ms, 1 s, 10 s, ...), so the quantiles are coarse: read them as "is it Fuseki or the API", not as precise numbers. Scoped by environment/stack only. Purple markers: dsp-api container restarts (deploys, but also crashes/reboots).

spec.title: Share of triplestore round trips slower than 100 ms / 1 s ($smoothing)
spec.description: Share of SPARQL round trips slower than 100 ms and than 1 s, Gravsearch vs everything else; rate() window = Smoothing window. Exact (bucket boundaries) and independent of traffic mix, so a step change is a real change. Scoped by environment/stack only. Purple markers: dsp-api container restarts (deploys, but also crashes/reboots).

spec.title: Triplestore round trips/s by query type ($smoothing)
spec.description: SPARQL round trips per second from dsp-api to Fuseki, by SPARQL form and the Gravsearch / maintenance flags, stacked; rate() window = Smoothing window. Scoped by environment/stack only.

spec.title: Requests per route ($smoothing)
spec.description: Requests per second per route, stacked; same filters as the server-time panel above; rate() window = Smoothing window. The denominator for server time per route: server time that rises with requests is load, without them a slowdown. Purple markers: dsp-api container restarts (deploys, but also crashes/reboots).

spec.title: Server time per route group — busy seconds per second ($smoothing)
spec.description: Seconds of request processing per second per route group (same regexes as the Route group filter), stacked; rate() window = Smoothing window. Honours Method and Exclude routes; ignores the Route group filter by design. Compare with Requests per route group below. Purple markers: dsp-api container restarts (deploys, but also crashes/reboots).

spec.title: Requests per route group ($smoothing)
spec.description: Requests per second per route group, stacked; the denominator for the server-time panel above; rate() window = Smoothing window. Honours Method and Exclude routes; ignores the Route group filter by design. Purple markers: dsp-api container restarts (deploys, but also crashes/reboots).

spec.title: ${quantile:text} response duration by route group ($smoothing)
spec.description: Percentile (Percentile filter, default p95) of full-request duration per route group, same groups and filters as the average panel above; rate() window = Smoothing window. Where the average panel says a group got slower, this says whether all of it did or only its tail. Percentiles come from tapir_request_duration_seconds_bucket, scraped since ops-deploy#1434 (stage from 2026-09-21, prod from 2026-09-23 ~06:00 UTC); earlier ranges show no percentile data. Buckets: 5, 10, 25, 50, 75, 100, 250, 500, 750 ms, 1, 2.5, 5, 7.5, 10, 15, 30, 45, 60 s; histogram_quantile() interpolates linearly inside a bucket and caps at 60 s. Log2 y-axis. Purple markers: dsp-api container restarts (deploys, but also crashes/reboots).

spec.title: ${quantile:text} response duration by route ($smoothing)
spec.description: Percentile (Percentile filter, default p95) of full-request duration per route, within the Route group / Route (path) / Exclude filters; rate() window = Smoothing window. Rare routes are noisy at high percentiles: with a handful of requests per window p99 is effectively the slowest request. Percentiles come from tapir_request_duration_seconds_bucket, scraped since ops-deploy#1434 (stage from 2026-09-21, prod from 2026-09-23 ~06:00 UTC); earlier ranges show no percentile data. Buckets: 5, 10, 25, 50, 75, 100, 250, 500, 750 ms, 1, 2.5, 5, 7.5, 10, 15, 30, 45, 60 s; histogram_quantile() interpolates linearly inside a bucket and caps at 60 s. Log2 y-axis. Purple markers: dsp-api container restarts (deploys, but also crashes/reboots).
